decisions.quote: In this replication and extension study, students’ attitude in introductory chemistry courses, including a chemistry course designed for nursing and allied health students, was measured using the Attitude toward the Subject of Chemistry Inventory. Results show that a low-involvement hierarchy of attitude effect for students’ attitude toward chemistry, previously observed after 5 weeks, persists throughout a semester, and is likely widespread in classes across our department.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files were checked and do not exist (never-adjudicated work). The supplied primary source consists solely of the title, author list, and abstract, with no in-text citations or reference list. Although the abstract explicitly describes a replication and extension study testing whether a low-involvement hierarchy of attitude effect previously observed after 5 weeks persists throughout a semester, it provides no bibliographic information (authors, year, title, or DOI) for that earlier study. Consequently, the available primary source evidence cannot establish the original work's identity or determine whether the retested 5-week finding is the supplied shipped row 134 (Ross, Nuñez, & Lai, 2018, 10.1039/c7rp00238f) or a different unshipped report.
